speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to examine a specific skin lesion you are concerned about. Can you describe its size, shape, color, and whether it has changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC).

The presentation of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penis in a 62-year-old male smoker is highly suspicious for penile SCC, and the concurrent lesion on your finger suggests potential cutaneous SCC or metastasis from the primary site. Given your history of smoking and failed treatments for syphilis and eczema, I need to confirm the diagnosis immediately. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the penile lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the penile and digital lesions.
